notes: §1985:VII.3.7.4 GR2: "Integer-1 or the value of the data item referenced by data-name-1 specifies the number of lines that can be written and/or spaced on the logical page. The value must be greater than zero." The LINAGE code has no edition arm; 85 reaches the members the 2023 rules use. BindLinageClause keeps integer-1 or data-name-1 as the page body operand, ResolveLinage resolves the data-name, the IntegerOperandRules.Slots row for the clause refuses a literal 0 (COBOL2386, probed), and LinageArg passes the operand's value with every OPEN and WRITE. BeginLinagePage (OPEN OUTPUT) and BeginNextLogicalPage (page overflow, ADVANCING PAGE) adopt the value through EvaluateLinage, and PositionOnLogicalPage overflows when LINAGE-COUNTER plus the lines advanced exceeds it, so written and spaced lines both count. Probed at 85: LINAGE 3 takes LINAGE-COUNTER 2, 3, then end-of-page and 1; ADVANCING 2 LINES under LINAGE 5 takes 3, 5, then end-of-page; data-name-1 moved from 2 to 3 after the OPEN gives a two-line first page and three-line pages after it. A data item holding zero, for which 1985 defines no result (2023 does, §2023:13.18.34.4 GR6: "If the value does not conform to these two rules, the EC-I-O-LINAGE exception condition is set to exist."), makes the OPEN or the overflowing WRITE unsuccessful through LinageViolationStatus (status 90, LINAGE-COUNTER 0, probed) and the run continues. The witness is LINAGE IS 2 LINES: the first WRITE takes NOT AT END-OF-PAGE and the second AT END-OF-PAGE.

next.reason: 1985: "The value must be greater than zero."; 2023: "If the value does not conform to these two rules, the EC-I-O-LINAGE exception condition is set to exist.". Meaning, page body and greater-than-zero rule are kept, but 2023 now defines a result for a nonconforming page size: an exception condition, then fixed LINAGE-COUNTER and continuation behavior.
